clue.text: Lying down as quickly as possible

definitions.meaning: someone stretched out full length on the ground is lying ...
going at top speed, with every effort

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are idioms: prostrate on the floor, or running at maximum effort and speed.

clue.text: Anxious as guitar part not quite complete

parts.note: a fret is a ridge on a guitar's fingerboard

indicators.note: not quite means the word for complete stops one letter short

parts.note: full means complete, entire

explanation.surface: A musician is worried because a guitar component is unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: Fretful means worried and uneasy, given to constant fretting.

clue.text: Song about Zulu on in state

indicators.note: about means the song goes around the other letters

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera
Zulu is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for Z
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tune about the Zulu people is playing in some state.
explanation.definitionFit: Arizona is a state in the south-western USA.

clue.text: Suppose one will receive letter from Greeks

indicators.note: will receive means the word one takes in the Greek letter

parts.note: taken as written
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone guesses they will get a message from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to hold or express an opinion, to suppose or think.

clue.text: Watch perhaps seen in American magazine article

parts.note: Time is a famous US news magazine
a piece is an article in a publication

explanation.surface: A wristwatch is featured in an American magazine story.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch is one example of a device for keeping time, with clocks being others.

clue.text: Empty beer containers for these traders?

indicators.note: an empty word has its insides removed, so only the first and last letters of beer remain

parts.note: ewers are large jugs, vessels for holding liquid

explanation.surface: Discarded beer bottles suggest which tradespeople have been here.
explanation.walkthrough: Empty looks like an adjective on the containers; it acts on beer alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Brewers make and sell beer, so they are tradesmen in that drink, as the question mark concedes.

clue.text: Be a really good person — or cruel and brutal one!

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
ST abbreviates saint, a person of great virtue

explanation.surface: An exhortation to virtue, or else a warning against savagery.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a moral choice between good and bad; the first half simply spells out its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A beast is a savage, brutish person, likened to a wild animal.

clue.text: Morse's first name and last always stated

indicators.note: stated means the words are spoken, so we want something said the same way

parts.note: last is the end, always is ever, together pronounced end-ever

explanation.surface: A fact about the detective Morse, and a remark about lasting forever.
explanation.walkthrough: Colin Dexter's Inspector Morse was revealed to have the first name Endeavour, also the title of the prequel series.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional Oxford detective Inspector Morse was christened Endeavour.

clue.text: Ruralite wrong to ditch large pot plant

indicators.note: wrong means the remaining letters are put in the wrong order and need rearranging
to ditch means the abbreviation for large is dropped from ruralite

explanation.surface: A country dweller errs in throwing away a big potted plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Pot plant looks like a houseplant; it is a pottery factory. Etruria was Josiah Wedgwood's pottery works in Stoke-on-Trent, an English pottery town.
explanation.definitionFit: Here a plant is a factory, and Wedgwood's Etruria works made pots.

clue.text: Playwright born an Algonquian speaker

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw was an Irish playwright
née means born, used before a maiden name

explanation.surface: A dramatist was born to speak a Native American language.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shawnee are a Native American people whose language belongs to the Algonquian family.

clue.text: Wanting best from Handel? It is magical

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows, spanning Handel, It, is and magical

explanation.surface: A music lover marvels at the enchanting quality of a Handel piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Elitism is the belief that only the top people or things deserve consideration, a desire for the very best.

clue.text: Small country on radar in revolt

indicators.note: letters in revolt have risen up and broken out of their order, so the words on radar are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebellion in a little nation shows up on the military's radar screens.
explanation.definitionFit: Andorra is a tiny principality in the Pyrenees between France and Spain.

clue.text: Vessel needing time on River Po

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another comes after it, so the time letter follows the rest

parts.note: a crossword favourite: a river is something that flows, a flow-er
the Italian river Po, taken as written

explanation.surface: A boat on the River Po needs some time to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: River looks like it goes with Po, as in the River Po; in fact it is the cryptic sense, a thing that flows, and Po stays as its own two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel is any container, and a pot for growing plants in is one.

clue.text: Item with Oedipal strings attached?

parts.note: a man too attached to his mother is said to be tied to her ... strings; Oedipus loved his mother

explanation.surface: Something offered with an unhealthy mother-fixation as a condition.
explanation.definitionFit: This kitchen garment is tied on with strings, and the idiom about mother-dependent sons names those strings.

clue.text: Drain to make white, not black

indicators.note: not tells us the black letter is left out of the whitening word

parts.note: to bleach is to whiten
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Instructions for emptying something to turn it white rather than dark.
explanation.definitionFit: To leach is to let liquid percolate out, draining a substance away from soil or material.

clue.text: Fine and well-built swimmer

parts.note: a hunky man is sturdy and muscular
the dory is a fish, and fish are crossword swimmers

explanation.surface: Praise for an athletic, muscular swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: Swimmer suggests a person in a pool; it is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunky-dory is informal for fine, satisfactory, all well.

clue.text: ESP in later years keeping old in secret work

parts.note: extrasensory perception, taken as written

indicators.note: keeping means the phrase about later years holds the abbreviation for old within it

parts.note: taken as written
one's later years are one's old age

explanation.surface: Someone develops psychic powers late in life and keeps it quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Spying is clandestine work gathering others' secrets.

clue.text: Servant concealing crime in holy residence

indicators.note: concealing means the servant hides the crime inside himself

parts.note: a page is a boy servant
arson is the crime of setting fires

explanation.surface: A household servant hides an offence in a sacred dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsonage is the house provided for a parish priest.

clue.text: One can relate well to race run poorly

indicators.note: done poorly, the letters of to race run end up badly ordered and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: An athlete identifies with anyone who has run a race badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Relate looks like sympathise; it means narrate, as in relating a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A gifted storyteller is someone skilled at relating anecdotes.

clue.text: Novel about British deposing leader in holy city

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: deposing leader means the holy city's first letter is removed

parts.note: Mecca is the holiest city of Islam

explanation.surface: A book about the British removing a ruler in a sacred city.
explanation.walkthrough: Novel could be an adjective meaning new; it is the noun, Daphne du Maurier's book.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebecca is Daphne du Maurier's celebrated 1938 novel.

clue.text: Michigan port appealingly elegant in the past

parts.note: chic means stylish and elegant
ago means in the past, as in long ago

explanation.surface: A harbour town in Michigan was once charmingly stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is a major port on the shore of Lake Michigan.

clue.text: Traitors getting round Spain's local taxes

indicators.note: getting round means the traitors surround the Spanish letter

parts.note: a rat is a betrayer or turncoat
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: Turncoats dodge the levies of a Spanish municipality.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain, the rates were the property tax paid to a local council before the council tax.

clue.text: Flow easily with crude oil making capital

parts.note: words that flow easily trip off the tongue

indicators.note: crude means rough and unrefined, so the letters of oil are put in a rough new order

explanation.surface: Crude oil runs freely from a wealthy nation's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Crude oil looks like one phrase; crude is the anagram signal for oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital city of Libya, an oil-producing state.

clue.text: Second goddess with vacant expression still here?

parts.note: Hebe was the Greek goddess of youth

indicators.note: vacant means the word expression is emptied, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a blank-faced goddess remains.
explanation.walkthrough: A shebeen is an unlicensed drinking den, chiefly Irish or Scottish, where home-distilled liquor might be sold; still is the distilling apparatus, not the adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: An illicit bar could house a still for making liquor, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Skating facility shortly opening by sea

indicators.note: opening means the word by is split apart to admit the shortened skating word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: shortly means the skating word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: an ice rink is where one skates

explanation.surface: An ice rink is soon to open at the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: The briny is a colloquial name for the sea, from its salty water.

clue.text: Tight one is come to cut back

indicators.note: tight is slang for drunk, and drunken letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A miserly person has come along to reduce spending.
explanation.walkthrough: Tight seems to describe a mean person, matching the definition; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To economise is to reduce spending, to trim expenses.

clue.text: Beer without head: that is disturbing

indicators.note: without head means the first letter of beer is dropped, like a beer with no froth

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A beer with no froth on top is a troubling sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and unsettling, giving an uneasy feeling.

clue.text: Character from Titanic holding up duck

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece holding up another sits above it, so duck comes first

parts.note: a duck is a score of zero in cricket, like the letter O
titanic means huge, as does mega

explanation.surface: Someone from the Titanic film is propping up a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: Titanic looks like the ship; it is the adjective meaning enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, a character in writing.

clue.text: Conservative-Liberal relationship brings outcry

parts.note: an amour is a love affair

explanation.surface: A coalition between Britain's Conservatives and Liberals provokes public protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamour is a loud protest or public demand.

clue.text: Impressive meow as Siamese at last moves

indicators.note: moves means these letters shift position into a new order
at last picks out the final letter of Siamese

explanation.surface: A Siamese cat's cry finally shifts, and it is striking.
explanation.definitionFit: Something awesome inspires awe, which is to say it is hugely impressive.

clue.text: Assistant wants line put into a flirtatious note

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: put into means the line letter is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: coy can mean coquettish, flirtatiously reticent
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An aide needs a line slipped into a teasing love letter.
explanation.walkthrough: Note looks like a written message; it is the musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: An acolyte is a helper, originally one assisting a priest at the altar.

clue.text: Row backed about Virginia's prevarication

indicators.note: about means the reversed noise goes around the state's letters
backed means the word for row is reversed, turned back to front

parts.note: a row is a din or noise
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A quarrel is reversed concerning someone's hedging.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasion is avoiding a straight answer, the essence of prevaricating.
